about: Adversarial KT matrix. Written 18 Oct before any output was seen. Each case is a short transcript run through the real pipeline (no LLM) by evaluation/matrix.py. Checks: shows / shows_any (normalised text visible somewhere in the document), absent / absent_re (not visible outside conflict warnings), never_alone (every document unit naming `text` also names `with`, so a superseded or hedged value is never shown on its own), verbatim (exact characters), in_section, order (same section, in order), flagged (shown in a conflict or gap warning), not_flagged (no conflict warning names both), coverage, completes, gaps_consistent (the PDF's Not Covered list names exactly the sections the coverage matrix calls Missing), sourced (no fact marked “no source”). level: must = a wrong final document; should = a desirable behaviour the product does not promise yet.

transcript: Our CI/CD pipeline starts when a developer raises a pull request. Jenkins builds the application, SonarQube checks code quality, and Trivy scans the container image before it is pushed to Amazon ECR. Deployment to Kubernetes happens through Helm. Production deployment requires approval from the release manager. If a critical vulnerability is detected, the release must not proceed until the issue is reviewed and resolved according to the security process. Developers maintain the pipeline, while the Platform team manages Kubernetes infrastructure. Rollback is supported through Helm, but the exact revision and emergency approval process are not documented. Pipeline failures generate Slack notifications. The team previously used manual deployments, but that process has been retired. We are planning to introduce automated rollback next quarter, although implementation has not started. cases.title: The user's KT 7 (an online learning platform, 25 Oct; checks written after reviewing its PDF): users using the product, a gap said as 'still undocumented', escalation contacts
transcript: Hi team, today I’m handing over our online learning platform. It serves around 20,000 active users daily. Students access the React application through CloudFront and an Application Load Balancer, which routes requests to services running on Amazon EKS. The backend uses Python FastAPI, PostgreSQL on Amazon RDS, and Redis for caching course information. GitHub Actions runs automated tests, Amazon ECR stores container images, and ArgoCD deploys releases to EKS. Terraform manages infrastructure. Prometheus and Grafana monitor application performance, while PagerDuty handles alerts. A common issue occurs when database connections are exhausted during examination periods. Check connection-pool usage and application errors before restarting services. Another issue is delayed video processing when background jobs accumulate in Amazon SQS. Database backups run daily and are retained for 14 days. Recovery testing is performed twice a year, but RTO and RPO have not been documented. Developers own application code, while Platform Engineering manages Kubernetes and deployment pipelines. Never modify Terraform state manually. The video-processing recovery procedure and formal escalation contacts are still undocumented.

texts: RTO and RPO have not been documented
